clue.text: This man was part ape

parts.note: points to the notorious skull-and-jaw hoax 'discovered' in Sussex in 1912, which paired a human cranium with an orangutan's jaw

explanation.walkthrough: Piltdown Man, a fake 'missing link' found in Sussex, England, really was part ape: the jawbone came from an orangutan.
explanation.definitionFit: The forged fossil man combined a human skull with an ape's jaw, so he literally was partly ape.

clue.text: No amateur villain can hold up parliament

parts.note: a pro, or professional, is no amateur
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: Only a seasoned crook could stall the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: To prorogue is to suspend a parliamentary session without dissolving it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proroguing discontinues a session of the legislature without dissolving it, halting its business.

clue.text: Figure of fun to one in Piccadilly Circus

definitions.text: Figure of fun to one in Piccadilly Circus

parts.words: Figure of fun to one in Piccadilly Circus
parts.note: the statue in Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros, god of Love, and the proverb says love laughs at a certain tradesman

explanation.walkthrough: The statue in London's Piccadilly Circus is known as Eros, i.e. Love, and the proverb runs 'Love laughs at locksmiths': no lock can keep lovers apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says love mocks these tradesmen, and Love stands on the fountain in London's famous square.

clue.text: "Borrowing the edge of husbandry" (Hamlet)

parts.note: Polonius's advice to Laertes, with the verb missing from the line 'borrowing ... the edge of husbandry'

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash between 'Borrowing' and 'the'. Polonius says 'borrowing dulls the edge of husbandry': lending and borrowing blunt thrift.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means blunts, and Polonius uses it to warn that borrowing weakens thrift.

clue.text: Horse's moribund part ?.

parts.note: names the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades, while also reading as a verb for fading away

explanation.walkthrough: The ridge between a horse's shoulder blades has this name, which also reads as 'dries up and dies', hence 'moribund'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridge at the base of a horse's neck carries this name, which as a verb means shrivels and decays.

clue.text: Humble craftsman, or a kind of bell fairy ?

explanation.surface: A lowly mender of pots, or perhaps a fairy of the bell variety.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition completes the name of Peter Pan's fairy, Tinker Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinker is an itinerant mender of pots and pans, a humble trade; Tinker Bell is the fairy in Peter Pan.

clue.text: Establish where Sir Joseph Porter passed his law exam

definitions.text: where Sir Joseph Porter passed his law exam

explanation.surface: Founding the place where a Gilbert and Sullivan admiral qualified.
explanation.walkthrough: In HMS Pinafore, Sir Joseph Porter sings 'I passed the examination at the Institute' before becoming First Lord of the Admiralty.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up or found is the verb sense; the noun is the college where the Pinafore character sat his law examination.

clue.text: Prophetic words

parts.note: the words revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, collected as Islam's scripture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prophetic' suggests prophecy; it means of the Prophet, Muhammad, whose revelations make up Islam's holy book.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam's holy book records revelations given to the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: They can make a horse go faster-or slower

definitions.text: They can make a horse go faster-or slower

parts.words: They can make a horse go faster-or slower
parts.note: spiked wheels on a rider's spurs urge a horse on, and the letters of 'slower' can be shuffled to spell them

explanation.walkthrough: Rowels are the spiked wheels on spurs that urge a horse on; 'or slower' adds that the same six letters rearrange from SLOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiked revolving wheels on a rider's spurs goad the mount into speeding up.

clue.text: Armed guard of the eastern kind, about 100

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for kind surrounds the numeral

parts.note: sort means kind
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: An oriental-style military detail, roughly a hundred strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SORT round C to give SCORT, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: An armed escort is a protective body of troops accompanying someone.

clue.text: XXXX ?

wordplay.reading: four X marks, X X X X

parts.note: a row of X marks, each the letter-writer's sign for a kiss

explanation.walkthrough: Each X at the end of a letter stands for a kiss, so four of them show someone kissing repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is the formal, Latinate verb for kissing, so a string of kiss marks shows that action.

clue.text: Salary of Archimedes for inventing one ?

explanation.surface: What did the Greek inventor get paid for his invention?
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a screw is a wage; the Archimedes screw is the water-raising device credited to him.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for wages or pay, and the Archimedean water pump is a spiral of that name.

clue.text: Love stormy seas, popular with ships of the desert

definitions.text: popular with ships of the desert

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, so the letter O

indicators.note: stormy seas are tossed about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who loves rough water, yet the sentence ends among camels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges SEAS into ASES, placed after O. 'Ships of the desert' are camels, and the places popular with them are watering holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels, poetically the ships of the desert, gather at fertile watering spots in the sand.

clue.text: Proposal in ale distribution gets us worked up

indicators.note: in places the proposal inside the rearranged letters
distribution spreads the letters of the word ale around into another order

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A motion is tabled while beer is handed round, and tempers rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' turns ALE into EAL; 'in' sets MOTION inside it, between E and AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stirred by strong feeling is agitated, the sense of being worked up.

clue.text: The dramatic ones !

parts.note: 'ones' reads as single units, and the drama's classical rules of time, place and action are a famous trio of them

explanation.walkthrough: Aristotle's three classical rules of drama, of time, place and action, are known by this name; 'ones' plays on oneness.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical drama theory demands three oneness rules: a single action, one place and one day.

clue.text: Cluelessness of the one Christian outstripped

explanation.surface: Lacking a clue, like the believer left behind in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: In Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, Christian and Hopeful walk ahead of a lad named Ignorance, who later is turned away from the Celestial City.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of knowledge is cluelessness, and Bunyan's allegory names the youth Christian leaves behind after that same quality.

clue.text: It's rum, anyway — it's obvious

indicators.note: any way the letters fall, so they are taken in a new order

parts.note: the contraction gives the letters I, T, S

explanation.surface: Tasting the drink and declaring that its oddness is self-evident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' rearranges the six letters of IT'S RUM. The definition is a whole statement: a self-evident remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude so plainly true it needs no saying is a statement that something is self-evident.

clue.text: What all good wine merchants do in Cheshire

definitions.text: What all good wine merchants do

explanation.surface: Advice to vintners in a north-west English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Good wine merchants keep fortified wine in stock; Stockport is a town historically in Cheshire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchants keep the fortified Portuguese wine on their shelves, and the same name belongs to a town near Manchester, once in Cheshire.

clue.text: In a confused rush premier includes one measure on top of another

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first group sits above the second ell
includes means the abbreviation holds the measure within it

parts.note: PM is the abbreviation for Prime Minister, the premier
an ell is an old measure of cloth length
another ell, a second of the same measure

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister, in a hurried muddle, stacks up measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts ELL inside PM; 'on top of' sets that group above a second ELL in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlong and disorderly haste is a confused rush.

clue.text: That's about the North-east corner of England's garden

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word surrounds the compass letters

parts.note: the word that, with 's as a link meaning is
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Pointing out the north-eastern corner of an English garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts THAT round NE: THA-NE-T. Kent is called 'the Garden of England', and the Isle of Thanet is its north-east corner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Thanet is the north-eastern tip of Kent, the county nicknamed the Garden of England.

clue.text: Scandal-school's nap-raiser

explanation.surface: A character from Sheridan's comedy who fluffs up cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Peter Teazle is the husband in Sheridan's play The School for Scandal; a teazle (teasel) is a prickly seed head used to raise the nap on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's comedy features the Teazle couple, and the plant's spiny heads were used to brush up fabric.

clue.text: Jules Verne captain is seen in one Scottish flower

indicators.note: is seen in places the captain inside the Scots word

parts.note: ane is the Scots word for one
Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A fictional submarine captain spotted inside a Scottish bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is seen in' puts NEMO inside ANE, after its A. 'Scottish flower' looks like one unit; 'Scottish' belongs to 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The windflower, with its cup-shaped blooms, is a garden plant in the buttercup family.

clue.text: Require a lady to do so ? That's mean!

definitions.text: Require a lady to do so ? That's mean!

parts.words: Require a lady to do so ? That's mean!
parts.note: split the word as a request that a lady declare her years, a rude thing to ask, while 'mean' is the arithmetic sense

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AVER AGE: making a lady state her age is mean (unkind), and the whole word means 'mean' in the arithmetic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean is the usual sense of the word, and making a woman declare her years is unkind.

clue.text: Old Copper Isle makes general presidential nomination

parts.note: D stood for the old British penny, a copper coin
the Isle of Wight lies off England's south coast

explanation.surface: An ancient coin and an island combine to put forward a presidential candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: D was the abbreviation for the pre-1971 British penny, a 'copper'. General Dwight D. Eisenhower became US President.
explanation.definitionFit: Eisenhower, a general, was nominated for president under his first name.

clue.text: It let loose a flood of scandal

definitions.text: It let loose a flood of scandal

parts.words: It let loose a flood of scandal
parts.note: a sluice that lets water out also names the Washington break-in affair that brought down Nixon

explanation.walkthrough: A sluice lets loose a flood of water; the Washington hotel complex gave its name to the 1970s scandal that unseated President Nixon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluice releases water, and the Nixon affair named after the Washington building unleashed a torrent of scandal.

clue.text: Cratchit Minimus takes gold from' the sea

parts.note: the youngest Cratchit in Dickens's A Christmas Carol is Tiny Tim; minimus is the school label for the youngest of brothers
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Tiny Tim plucks treasure from the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minimus' is the British public-school label for the youngest of brothers; the youngest Cratchit is Tiny Tim.
explanation.definitionFit: The Timor Sea lies between the island of that name and northern Australia.

clue.text: Belshazzar's notification of short weight

parts.note: the writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast in the Book of Daniel, one word of which means weighed and found wanting

explanation.walkthrough: In Daniel 5 the hand writes MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN; Daniel reads the third word as 'thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Biblical message on the wall, this word told the king he had been weighed and found lacking.

clue.text: A bit of a laugh having the governor in place of the driver

indicators.note: in puts the governor inside the place

parts.note: a golfer uses a driver club from the tee
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: Gentle mirth when the colonial governor takes the chauffeur's seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a chauffeur; it is a golf club, used from the TEE. 'in' puts HE inside TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates a suppressed giggle, a small snigger.

clue.text: Street arab put a leg in

parts.note: gam is slang for a leg
taken as written

explanation.surface: A street child told to stick a leg in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street arab' is an old term for a homeless urchin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old phrase for a ragged urchin living on city streets, which the French loanword also means.

clue.text: Cooked hot meal-so disgusting !

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about a hot dinner that turned out revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges the nine letters of HOT MEAL SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent and hateful is disgusting; both describe what provokes revulsion.

clue.text: Revolutionary artist ?

explanation.surface: A painter with radical politics.
explanation.walkthrough: A turner is literally one who revolves things, as on a lathe; J. M. W. Turner was the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who turns or revolves is literally revolutionary; J. M. W. Turner was a celebrated English painter.

clue.text: Bust supporter

parts.note: 'bust' suggests a bra, but here it is a sculpted head and shoulders standing on a plinth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust supporter' wants to be a brassiere; the bust is a sculpture, and it stands on a column base.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted head-and-shoulders portrait is displayed on a column or plinth beneath it.
